Theorem 7.3.

Let K⊂YK\subset Y be a null-homologous knot. There is a relatively graded isomorphism of groups

H∗​(𝕏^i,p/q)≅H​F^​(Yp/q​(K),i)H_{*}(\widehat{\mathbb{X}}_{i,p/q})\cong\widehat{HF}(Y_{p/q}(K),i)

for each i∈ℤ/p​ℤi\in\mathbb{Z}/{p}\mathbb{Z}.

7.2. Absolute gradings

In fact, Theorem 1.1 (and indeed Theorem 6.1) actually determines H​F+​(Yp/q​(K),i)HF^{+}(Y_{p/q}(K),i) as an absolutely graded group.

An absolute grading on 𝕏i,p/q+​(K){\mathbb{X}}^{+}_{i,p/q}(K) compatible with the relative grading is specified by fixing an absolute grading on B⌊i+p​sq⌋+{B}^{+}_{\lfloor\frac{i+ps}{q}\rfloor} (for any ss), thought of as a subcomplex of 𝕏i,p/q+​(K){\mathbb{X}}^{+}_{i,p/q}(K) (note that it is independent of the choice of KK). This absolute grading in turn is in turn determined by a grading on its homology H∗​(B⌊i+p​sq⌋+)≅𝒯+H_{*}({B}^{+}_{\lfloor\frac{i+ps}{q}\rfloor})\cong{\mathcal{T}}^{+}. Finally, that datum is fixed by the requirement H∗​(𝕏i,p/q+​(O))≅𝒯+H_{*}({\mathbb{X}}^{+}_{i,p/q}(O))\cong{\mathcal{T}}^{+} in such a way that its bottom-most non-trivial element is supported in dimension d⁡(Sp/q3​(O),i)=d⁡(L⁡(p,q),i)d(S^{3}_{p/q}(O),i)=d(L(p,q),i). (Explicit, recursive formulas for these rational numbers can be found in Proposition  of [17].)

This assertion follows easily from the proof of Theorem 1.1. Specifically, as in Subsection 6.3, the composite of

f1δ:C​Fδ​(Yλ​(K))⟶C​Fδ​(Yn​k⋅μ+λ​(K))f^{\delta}_{1}\colon CF^{\delta}(Y_{\lambda}(K))\longrightarrow CF^{\delta}(Y_{nk\cdot\mu+\lambda}(K))

with the projection onto C​Fδ​(Yn​k⋅μ+λ​(K),𝔱)⊂C​Fδ​(Yn​k⋅μ+λ​(K))CF^{\delta}(Y_{nk\cdot\mu+\lambda}(K),\mathfrak{t})\subset CF^{\delta}(Y_{nk\cdot\mu+\lambda}(K)) is a homogeneous map (provided that nn is sufficiently large). Moreover, its degree depends on the intersection form of the cobordism X⁡(k)X(k) and the first Chern class of 𝔱\mathfrak{t}. Moreover, the proof of Theorem 6.4 shows that this map is also identified with the projection 𝕏𝔰δ​(λ)⟶Aξδ​(Y,K¯){\mathbb{X}}^{\delta}_{\mathfrak{s}}(\lambda)\longrightarrow{A}^{\delta}_{\xi}(Y,\overline{K}). Since the intersection form of X⁡(k)X(k) does not depend on the particular knot K¯\overline{K}, the claim follows.

8. Knots which admit LL-space surgeries

Suppose that K⊂S3K\subset S^{3} is a knot which admits an LL-space surgery with positive slope rr. Examples of such knots include all torus knots, and also knots from Berge’s list, c.f. [1]. Moreover, an alternating knot KK with unknotting number equal to one gives rise to another knot C⊂S3C\subset S^{3} which admits an LL-space surgery. This new knot CC is obtained by performing the unknotting operation, but connecting the two strands which were crossed by an arc γ\gamma; CC then is the branched double-cover γ\gamma, compare [15].

Theorem 1.2 says that for such a knot, the Alexander polynomial is determined from the correction terms. In this application, we find it convenient to use the group H​F+HF^{+}; to do this, recall the characterization of LL-spaces in terms of this group [16]: a rational homology three-sphere YY is an LL-space if and only if for each 𝔱∈Spinc​(Y)\mathfrak{t}\in{\mathrm{Spin}}^{c}(Y),

H​F+​(Y,𝔱)≅𝒯+.HF^{+}(Y,\mathfrak{t})\cong{\mathcal{T}}^{+}.

The correction terms d⁡(Y,𝔱)d(Y,\mathfrak{t}) of an LL-space is the minimal grading of any homogeneous element of H​F+​(Y,𝔱)HF^{+}(Y,\mathfrak{t}).

The symmetrized Alexander polynomial ΔK​(T)\Delta_{K}(T) plays a role, since it is the Euler characteristic of the knot Floer homology; i.e.

∑sχ⁡(H^​F​K∗​(S3,K,s))⋅Ts=ΔK​(T),\sum_{s}\chi(\widehat{H}FK_{*}(S^{3},K,s))\cdot T^{s}=\Delta_{K}(T),

c.f. Equation () of [22] or [27].

Proof of Theorem 1.2. It is easy to see that both maps vs+:H∗​(As+)⟶H∗​(B+)v^{+}_{s}\colon H_{*}({A}^{+}_{s})\longrightarrow H_{*}({B}^{+}) and hs+:H∗​(As+)⟶H∗​(B+)h^{+}_{s}\colon H_{*}({A}^{+}_{s})\longrightarrow H_{*}({B}^{+}) are surjective, since B+≅H​F+​(S3){B}^{+}\cong HF^{+}(S^{3}), and both maps are isomorphisms in all sufficiently large degrees.

Fix i∈ℤ/p​ℤi\in\mathbb{Z}/{p}\mathbb{Z}, and let s∈ℤs\in\mathbb{Z} be an arbitrary representative. Split 𝔸i+=As+⊕J{\mathbb{A}}^{+}_{i}={A}^{+}_{s}\oplus J where J=⨁t≠sA⌊i+s​pq⌋+J=\bigoplus_{t\neq s}{A}^{+}_{\lfloor\frac{i+sp}{q}\rfloor}. From the above remarks, it is clear that the restriction of Di,p/q+D^{+}_{i,p/q} to H∗​(J)H_{*}(J) surjects onto H∗​(𝔹i+)H_{*}({\mathbb{B}}^{+}_{i}). It follows at once that there is a surjection

φ:Ker(H∗(Di,p/q+):H∗(𝔸i+)⟶H∗(𝔹i+))⟶H∗(As+).\varphi\colon\mathrm{Ker}\left(H_{*}(D^{+}_{i,p/q})\colon H_{*}({\mathbb{A}}^{+}_{i})\longrightarrow H_{*}({\mathbb{B}}^{+}_{i})\right)\longrightarrow H_{*}({A}^{+}_{s}).

Moreover, it follows from this surjectivity, combined with Theorem 1.1, that

Ker(H∗(Di,p/q+):H∗(𝔸i+)⟶H∗(𝔹i+))≅HF+(Sp/q3(K),i)≅𝒯+.\mathrm{Ker}\left(H_{*}(D^{+}_{i,p/q})\colon H_{*}({\mathbb{A}}^{+}_{i})\longrightarrow H_{*}({\mathbb{B}}^{+}_{i})\right)\cong HF^{+}(S^{3}_{p/q}(K),i)\cong{\mathcal{T}}^{+}.

The surjectivity of φ\varphi, together with the fact that H∗​(As+)≅H∗​(B+)H_{*}({A}^{+}_{s})\cong H_{*}({B}^{+}) in all sufficiently large degree combine to show that H∗​(As+)⊗ℤℚ≅𝒯+⊗ℤℚH_{*}({A}^{+}_{s})\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}\cong{\mathcal{T}}^{+}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}. Applying the same argument, only taking coefficients in ℤ/p​ℤ\mathbb{Z}/{p}\mathbb{Z} for arbitrary pp shows that H∗​(As+)≅𝒯+H_{*}({A}^{+}_{s})\cong{\mathcal{T}}^{+}.

Having established that H∗​(As+)≅𝒯+H_{*}({A}^{+}_{s})\cong{\mathcal{T}}^{+}, and that vs+v^{+}_{s} and hs+h^{+}_{s} are isomorphisms in all sufficiently large degrees, it follows that vs+v^{+}_{s} is modeled on multiplication by UVsU^{V_{s}}, and hs+h^{+}_{s} is multiplication by UHsU^{H_{s}}, where all Vs,Hs≥0V_{s},H_{s}\geq 0.

The condition that Ker(H∗(Di,p/q+):H∗(𝔸i+)⟶H∗(𝔹i+))≅𝒯+\mathrm{Ker}\left(H_{*}(D^{+}_{i,p/q})\colon H_{*}({\mathbb{A}}^{+}_{i})\longrightarrow H_{*}({\mathbb{B}}^{+}_{i})\right)\cong{\mathcal{T}}^{+} ensures readily that in each i∈ℤ/p​ℤi\in\mathbb{Z}/{p}\mathbb{Z}, there can be at most one integer s∈ℤs\in\mathbb{Z} for which both V⌊i+p​sq⌋V_{\lfloor\frac{i+ps}{q}\rfloor} and H⌊i+p​sq⌋≥0H_{\lfloor\frac{i+ps}{q}\rfloor}\geq 0. Our aim now is to determine which value of ss has this property.

Let m⁡(s)=min⁡(Vs,Hs)m(s)=\min(V_{s},H_{s}). We claim that

(29) m⁡(s1)≤m⁡(s2)\displaystyle m(s_{1})\leq m(s_{2}) if s1≤s2≤0​or​s1≥s2≥0.\displaystyle s_{1}\leq s_{2}\leq 0~\text{or}~s_{1}\geq s_{2}\geq 0.

To this end, we have an exact sequence

0→C{i<0andj≥s}→C​{max⁡(i,j−s)}→v+C{i≥0}→0.\begin{CD}0@>{}>{}>C\{i<0~\text{and}~j\geq s\}@>{}>{}>C\{\max(i,j-s)\}@>{v^{+}}>{}>C\{i\geq 0\}@>{}>{}>0.\end{CD}

Since χ⁡(H^​F​K​(K,s))=as\chi(\widehat{H}FK(K,s))=a_{s}, it follows at once that for s≥0s\geq 0,

χ(C{i<0andj≥s})=ts(K),\chi(C\{i<0~\text{and}~j\geq s\})=t_{s}(K),

which in turn is the same as VsV_{s}. Similarly, χ(C{i≥0andj<s})=ts(K)+2s\chi(C\{i\geq 0~\text{and}~j<s\})=t_{s}(K)+2s, which is HsH_{s}. In particular, this (together with a symmetric argument for s≤0s\leq 0) shows that

(30) Vs≤Hs​for​s≥0\displaystyle V_{s}\leq H_{s}~\text{for}~s\geq 0 and Vs≥Hs​for​s≤0.\displaystyle V_{s}\geq H_{s}~\text{for}~s\leq 0.

Incidentally, we have just established that

(31) ts=m⁡(s)≥0.t_{s}=m(s)\geq 0.

Note that there is a natural quotient map As+⟶As+1+{A}^{+}_{s}\longrightarrow{A}^{+}_{s+1}, and indeed, the projection of As+⟶Bs+{A}^{+}_{s}\longrightarrow{B}^{+}_{s} factors through this quotient. It follows at once that {Vs}s∈ℤ\{V_{s}\}_{s\in\mathbb{Z}} is a non-increasing sequence in ss. Dually, {Hs}s∈ℤ\{H_{s}\}_{s\in\mathbb{Z}} is an non-decreasing sequence in ss. Combining this with Equation (30), Equation (29) follows.

Having established that for each i∈ℤ/p​ℤi\in\mathbb{Z}/{p}\mathbb{Z}, there is exactly one non-zero integer among the {m⁡(⌊i+p​sq⌋)}s∈ℤ\{m(\lfloor\frac{i+ps}{q}\rfloor)\}_{s\in\mathbb{Z}}, Equation (29) together with the fact that m⁡(s)=m⁡(−s)m(s)=m(-s) (an easy consequence of Equation (31)) shows that m⁡(⌊iq⌋)≠0m(\lfloor\frac{i}{q}\rfloor)\neq 0 implies that

|⌊iq⌋|≤|⌊p2​q⌋|\Big|\lfloor\frac{i}{q}\rfloor\Big|\leq\Big|\lfloor\frac{p}{2q}\rfloor\Big|

for all s∈ℤs\in\mathbb{Z}.

Finally, note that the bottom-most generator of A⌊iq⌋+{A}^{+}_{\lfloor\frac{i}{q}\rfloor} is an element whose degree is 2​m​(⌊iq⌋)2m(\lfloor\frac{i}{q}\rfloor) less than the corresponding generator for the unknot. In view of the remarks from Subsection 7.2, the theorem now follows. ∎

Lemma 8.1.

Let K⊂S3K\subset S^{3} be a knot. The map vs+:As+⟶B+v^{+}_{s}\colon{A}^{+}_{s}\longrightarrow{B}^{+} is an isomorphism on homology for all s≥0s\geq 0 if and only if H^​F​K​(K,s)=0\widehat{H}FK(K,s)=0 for all s>0s>0.

Proof. It is easy to see by descending induction on ss that vs+v^{+}_{s} is an isomorphism on homology for all s≥ds\geq d if and only if H^​F​K​(K,s)=0\widehat{H}FK(K,s)=0 for all s>ds>d.           

Proof of Corollary 1.3. Suppose that Sp/q3​(K)≅Sp/q3​(O)S^{3}_{p/q}(K)\cong S^{3}_{p/q}(O). Then, for some permutation σ:ℤ/p​ℤ⟶ℤ/p​ℤ\sigma\colon\mathbb{Z}/{p}\mathbb{Z}\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z}/{p}\mathbb{Z}, we have that H​F+​(Sp/q3​(O),i)≅H​F+​(Sp/q3​(K),σ⁡(i))HF^{+}(S^{3}_{p/q}(O),i)\cong HF^{+}(S^{3}_{p/q}(K),\sigma(i)) for all ii. It follows from the proof of Theorem 1.2 (Equation (31)) that ti​(K)≥0t_{i}(K)\geq 0 for all ii. Summing Equation 2 over all ii and using the hypothesis that Sp/q3​(K)≅Sp/q3​(O)S^{3}_{p/q}(K)\cong S^{3}_{p/q}(O), we conclude that ti​(K)≡0t_{i}(K)\equiv 0. It follows that Vs=0V_{s}=0 for s≥0s\geq 0, i.e. vs+:H∗​(As+)⟶H​F+​(S3)v^{+}_{s}\colon H_{*}({A}^{+}_{s})\longrightarrow HF^{+}(S^{3}) is an isomorphism for all s≥0s\geq 0. According to Lemma 8.1, H^​F​K​(K,s)=0\widehat{H}FK(K,s)=0 for all s≠0s\neq 0, and hence, according to [21], KK is the unknot. ∎

9. On cosmetic surgeries

Under favorable circumstances, the existence of an orientation-preserving homeomorphism H​F^​(Sr3​(K))≅H​F^​(Ss3​(K))\widehat{HF}(S^{3}_{r}(K))\cong\widehat{HF}(S^{3}_{s}(K)) for distinct rr and ss forces the knot Floer homology of KK to agree with that for the unknot, and hence for the knot to be unknotted. This is not always the case, though. For example, the knot K=944K=9_{44} has the property that H​F+​(S+13​(K))≅H​F+​(S−13​(K))HF^{+}(S^{3}_{+1}(K))\cong HF^{+}(S^{3}_{-1}(K)), although S+13​(K)≇S−13​(K)S^{3}_{+1}(K)\not\cong S^{3}_{-1}(K). Specifically, according to Theorem  of [26], the knot 9449_{44} has

H^​F​K​(K,i)=ℤ(i)|ai|\widehat{H}FK(K,i)=\mathbb{Z}^{|a_{i}|}_{(i)}

where the subscript indicates the degree in which the summand is supported, and aia_{i} is the it​hi^{th} coefficient of the Alexander polynomial

ΔK​(T)=∑i∈ℤai⋅Ti=T−2−4​T−1+7−4​T+T2.\Delta_{K}(T)=\sum_{i\in\mathbb{Z}}a_{i}\cdot T^{i}=T^{-2}-4T^{-1}+7-4T+T^{2}.

It is now a straightforward application of the surgery formula, either in the form given in the present paper or from [25], that

H​F+​(S+13​(K))≅𝒯(0)+⊕ℤ(0)2⊕ℤ(−1)2≅H​F+​(S−13​(K)).HF^{+}(S^{3}_{+1}(K))\cong{\mathcal{T}}^{+}_{(0)}\oplus\mathbb{Z}_{(0)}^{2}\oplus\mathbb{Z}_{(-1)}^{2}\cong HF^{+}(S^{3}_{-1}(K)).

On the other hand, Walter Neumann [13] informs us that the manifolds S+13​(K)S^{3}_{+1}(K) and S−13​(K)S^{3}_{-1}(K) can be distinguished (using the computer program Snap [3], see also [31]) by their hyperbolic volume; one has hyperbolic volume roughly 5.525.52, the other has hyperbolic volume roughly 5.275.27.

Our results here can be proved by restricting attention to Floer homology with coefficients in any field 𝔽\mathbb{F}, which we suppress from the notation. For concreteness, we restrict to 𝔽=ℤ/2​ℤ\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{Z}/{2}\mathbb{Z}, so that e.g. H​F^​(S3)\widehat{HF}(S^{3}) denotes the homology H∗​(C​F^​(S3)⊗ℤ𝔽)H_{*}(\widehat{CF}(S^{3})\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{F}).

Definition 9.1.

Define ν⁡(K)\nu(K) by

ν(K)=min{s∈ℤ|v^s:A^s⟶C​F^(S3)induces a non-trivial map in homology}.\nu(K)=\min\{s\in\mathbb{Z}\big|\widehat{v}_{s}\colon\widehat{A}_{s}\longrightarrow\widehat{CF}(S^{3})~\text{induces a non-trivial map in homology}\}.
Lemma 9.2.

If K⊂S3K\subset S^{3} and −K-{K} denotes its reflection, then either ν⁡(K)\nu(K) or ν⁡(−K)\nu(-{K}) is non-negative.

Proof. Let {ℱs}s∈ℤ\{\mathcal{F}_{s}\}_{s\in\mathbb{Z}} be the knot filtration of C​F^​(S3)\widehat{CF}(S^{3}) (i.e. in the notation of Section 3 ℱs=Cξ0{j<s}\mathcal{F}_{s}=C_{\xi_{0}}\{j<s\}, where ξ0∈Spinc¯​(S3,K)\xi_{0}\in\underline{{\mathrm{Spin}}^{c}}(S^{3},K) is the relative Spinc{\mathrm{Spin}}^{c} structure with trivial first Chern class) and let

τ⁡(K)=min⁡{s∈ℤ|H∗​(ℱs)⟶H​F^​(S3)​is non-trivial}.\tau(K)=\min\{s\in\mathbb{Z}\big|H_{*}(\mathcal{F}_{s})\longrightarrow\widehat{HF}(S^{3})~\text{is non-trivial}\}.

Recall that τ⁡(K)=−τ⁡(−K)\tau(K)=-\tau(-{K}) and also that ν⁡(K)=τ⁡(K)\nu(K)=\tau(K) or τ⁡(K)+1\tau(K)+1 (c.f. Lemma  of [18] and Proposition  from the same refence respectively; or alternatively, see [27]).           

The integer ν⁡(K)\nu(K) dictates the maps on homology induced by all the h^s\widehat{h}_{s} and v^s\widehat{v}_{s}, according to the following two lemmas.

Lemma 9.3.

For all s≥ν⁡(K)s\geq\nu(K), v^s\widehat{v}_{s} induces a non-trivial map in homology.

Proof. This follows at once from the fact that the image of v^s\widehat{v}_{s} is ℱs\mathcal{F}_{s}, and ℱs⊆ℱt\mathcal{F}_{s}\subseteq\mathcal{F}_{t} if s≤ts\leq t.           

Lemma 9.4.

If ν⁡(K)≥0\nu(K)\geq 0, then for all s>0s>0, (h^s)∗=0(\widehat{h}_{s})_{*}=0.

Proof. The image of h^s:A^s⟶B^\widehat{h}_{s}\colon\widehat{A}_{s}\longrightarrow\widehat{B} is identified with ℱ−s⊂B^\mathcal{F}_{-s}\subset\widehat{B}, thus, if s>0s>0 and τ⁡(K)≥0\tau(K)\geq 0, then the map on homology induced by h^s\widehat{h}_{s} is trivial.           

Proposition 9.5.

Let K⊂S3K\subset S^{3} be a knot, and fix a pair of relatively prime integers pp and qq. Then

(32) rk​H​F^​(Sp/q3​(K))=|p|+2​max⁡(0,(2​ν​(K)−1)​|q|−|p|)+|q|​(∑s(rk​H∗​(A^s)−1))\mathrm{rk}\widehat{HF}(S^{3}_{p/q}(K))=|p|+2\max(0,(2\nu(K)-1)|q|-|p|)+|q|\left(\sum_{s}\left(\mathrm{rk}H_{*}(\widehat{A}_{s})-1\right)\right)

Proof. Recall that if K⊂S3K\subset S^{3}, and −K-{K} denotes its reflection, then Sr3​(K)≅−S−r3​(−K)S^{3}_{r}(K)\cong-S^{3}_{-r}(-{K}). Thus, in view of Lemma 9.2 and Equation (33), we can assume without loss of generality that ν⁡(K)≥0\nu(K)\geq 0. Also, of course, we can assume that q≥0q\geq 0. Using Theorem 7.3 to express H​F^​(Sp/q3​(K))\widehat{HF}(S^{3}_{p/q}(K)) in terms of H∗​(𝕏^p/q)H_{*}(\widehat{\mathbb{X}}_{p/q}), calculating the rank of H∗​(𝕏^p/q)H_{*}(\widehat{\mathbb{X}}_{p/q}) is now straightforward application of Lemmas 9.3 and 9.4. In fact, the cokernel D^{\widehat{D}} has rank max⁡(0,(2​ν​(K)−1)​q−p)\max(0,(2\nu(K)-1)q-p), while its kernel has rank

p+max⁡(0,(2​ν​(K)−1)​q−p)+q⁡(∑s(rk​H∗​(A^s)−1)).p+\max(0,(2\nu(K)-1)q-p)+q\left(\sum_{s}\left(\mathrm{rk}H_{*}(\widehat{A}_{s})-1\right)\right).

       

(The above proposition holds even in the case where pp and qq are not relatively prime, with the understanding that if (p,q)=a(p,q)=a, then H​F^​(Sp/q3​(K))\widehat{HF}(S^{3}_{p/q}(K)) denotes the direct sum of aa many copies of H​F^​(Sp′/q′3​(K))\widehat{HF}(S^{3}_{p^{\prime}/q^{\prime}}(K)), where here p′=p/ap^{\prime}=p/a, q′=q/aq^{\prime}=q/a.)

The following result is analogous to Lemma 8.1.

Proposition 9.6.

Let KK be a knot with ν⁡(K)=0\nu(K)=0 and rk​H∗​(A^s​(K))=1\mathrm{rk}H_{*}(\widehat{A}_{s}(K))=1 for all s∈ℤs\in\mathbb{Z}. Then, KK is the unknot. More generally,

g⁡(K)=max⁡(ν⁡(K),{s∈ℤ|rk​H∗​(A^s−1)>1}).g(K)=\max(\nu(K),\{s\in\mathbb{Z}\big|\mathrm{rk}H_{*}(\widehat{A}_{s-1})>1\}).

Proof. Recall [21] that

g⁡(K)=max⁡{t∈ℤ|H^​F​K​(K,t)≠0}.g(K)=\max\{t\in\mathbb{Z}\big|\widehat{H}FK(K,t)\neq 0\}.

This readily implies that the map v^:A^s⟶C​F^​(S3)\widehat{v}\colon\widehat{A}_{s}\longrightarrow\widehat{CF}(S^{3}) induces an isomorphism in homology for all s≥g⁡(K)s\geq g(K): A^s\widehat{A}_{s} has a subcomplex C​{i<0,j=s}C\{i<0,j=s\}, the kernel of v^s\widehat{v}_{s}, which is easily seen to be acyclic (as it is filtered by subcomplexes whose associated graded has homology isomorphic to ⨁t>sH^​F​K​(K,t)\bigoplus_{t>s}\widehat{H}FK(K,t)), and moreover its image in C{i=0}C\{i=0\} consists of the subcomplex C​{i=0,j≤s}C\{i=0,j\leq s\}, whose quotient is acyclic.

Thus, we have proved that

g⁡(K)≥max⁡(ν⁡(K),{s∈ℤ|rk​H∗​(A^s)>1}CLOSE.g(K)\geq\max(\nu(K),\{s\in\mathbb{Z}\big|\mathrm{rk}H_{*}(\widehat{A}_{s})>1\}.

Now consider

0→C⁡{i<0,j≥g−1}→C{max(i,j−g+1)≥0}→vg−1+C{i≥0}→0,\begin{CD}0@>{}>{}>C\{i<0,j\geq g-1\}@>{}>{}>C\{\max(i,j-g+1)\geq 0\}@>{v^{+}_{g-1}}>{}>C\{i\geq 0\}@>{}>{}>0,\end{CD}

where the midddle term here is, of course Ag−1+{A}^{+}_{g-1}. Since H​F​K​(K,t)=H∗​(C⁡{(0,t)})=0HFK(K,t)=H_{*}(C\{(0,t)\})=0 for all t>gt>g, it follows from the natural filtration that H∗(C{i<0j≥g−1})≅H∗({(−1,g−1)})≅H∗(C{0,g})=H^FK(K,g)≠0H_{*}(C\{i<0j\geq g-1\})\cong H_{*}(\{(-1,g-1)\})\cong H_{*}(C\{0,g\})=\widehat{H}FK(K,g)\neq 0. It follows at once that v^g−1\widehat{v}_{g-1} is not an isomorphism. It follows at once that either the map is not surjective, in which case ν⁡(K)=g−1\nu(K)=g-1, or it has kernel, in which case rk​H∗​(A^g−1)>1\mathrm{rk}H_{*}(\widehat{A}_{g-1})>1.           

Before stating the next result, we recall that the total rank of H​F^​(Y)\widehat{HF}(Y) is independent of the orientation of YY:

(33) rk​H​F^​(−Y)=rk​H​F^​(Y).\mathrm{rk}\widehat{HF}(-Y)=\mathrm{rk}\widehat{HF}(Y).

(Indeed, in Proposition  of [23], it is shown that H​F^∗​(−Y)≅H​F^∗​(Y)\widehat{HF}^{*}(-Y)\cong\widehat{HF}_{*}(Y).)

Theorem 9.7.

Let K⊂S3K\subset S^{3} be a knot, and suppose that rr and ss are distinct rational numbers with the property that Sr3​(K)≅±Ss3​(K)S^{3}_{r}(K)\cong\pm S^{3}_{s}(K). Then, either Sr3​(K)S^{3}_{r}(K) is an LL-space, or rr and ss have opposite signs.

Proof. Since H1(S±p/q3(K);ℤ)≅ℤ/pℤH_{1}(S^{3}_{\pm p/q}(K);\mathbb{Z})\cong\mathbb{Z}/{p}\mathbb{Z}, we can fix pp throughout. Now, according to Proposition 9.5, for fixed pp, and positive integral qq, rk​H​F^​(Sp/q3​(K))\mathrm{rk}\widehat{HF}(S^{3}_{p/q}(K)) is a monotone non-decreasing function of qq. In fact, the function is strictly monotone except possibly for sufficiently small qq, for which the rank is pp. But this ensures that Sp/q3​(K)S^{3}_{p/q}(K) is an LL-space. The same remarks hold for the function rkH​F^(S−p/q3(K))\mathrm{rk}\widehat{HF}(S^{3}_{-p/q}(K)) for fixed pp and positive, integral qq. Since the total rank of H​F^​(Y)\widehat{HF}(Y) is an invariant of the underlying (unoriented) three-manifold, c.f. Equation (33), the result holds.           

Proposition 9.8.

If KK is a non-trivial knot with ν⁡(K)=0\nu(K)=0, then if there are rational numbers r,s∈ℚr,s\in\mathbb{Q} with r≠sr\neq s and Sr3​(K)≅Ss3​(K)S^{3}_{r}(K)\cong S^{3}_{s}(K), then r=±sr=\pm s.

Proof. According to Proposition 9.5, if rk​H​F^​(Sp/q3​(K))=rk​H​F^​(Sp/q′3​(K))\mathrm{rk}\widehat{HF}(S^{3}_{p/q}(K))=\mathrm{rk}\widehat{HF}(S^{3}_{p/q^{\prime}}(K)) for q′≠±qq^{\prime}\neq\pm q, then rk​H∗​(A^s)=1\mathrm{rk}H_{*}(\widehat{A}_{s})=1 for all ss. Now, in view of Proposition 9.6, KK is the unknot, contrary to our assumption. Thus, it follows that for a cosmetic surgery on KK, r=−sr=-s.           

Theorem 9.9.

Let K⊂S3K\subset S^{3} be a knot with Seifert genus equal to one. Then if Sr3​(K)≅Ss3​(K)S^{3}_{r}(K)\cong S^{3}_{s}(K) as oriented manifolds, then either Sr3​(K)S^{3}_{r}(K) is an LL-space or r=sr=s.

Proof. In view of Theorem 9.7, we can assume that r>0r>0 and s<0s<0.

As in the proof of Proposition 9.6, it is clear that

v^s:H∗​(A^s​(K))⟶H​F^​(S3)\widehat{v}_{s}\colon H_{*}(\widehat{A}_{s}(K))\longrightarrow\widehat{HF}(S^{3})

is an isomorphism for all s>0s>0. Also, ν⁡(K)≤1\nu(K)\leq 1.

We exclude the possibility that ν⁡(K)=1\nu(K)=1. For Sr3​(K)S^{3}_{r}(K), we have that in any given Spinc{\mathrm{Spin}}^{c} structure, H​F^​(Sr3​(K),𝔱)\widehat{HF}(S^{3}_{r}(K),\mathfrak{t}) is described by

H∗​(A^0​(K))m⊕𝔽m−1.H_{*}(\widehat{A}_{0}(K))^{m}\oplus\mathbb{F}^{m-1}.

Since this group is also described as the Floer homology of Ss3​(K)S^{3}_{s}(K) with negative ss, it has the form

H∗​(A^0​(K))n⊕𝔽n+1.H_{*}(\widehat{A}_{0}(K))^{n}\oplus\mathbb{F}^{n+1}.

Since rk​H∗​(A^0​(K))≠0\mathrm{rk}H_{*}(\widehat{A}_{0}(K))\neq 0 (since its Euler characteristic is 11), the equality of these two ranks forces at once that m=n+1m=n+1 and rk​H∗​(A^0​(K))=1\mathrm{rk}H_{*}(\widehat{A}_{0}(K))=1. But it is easy to see that a relatively graded isomorphism

H∗​(A^0​(K))n+1⊕𝔽(−1)n≅H∗​(A^0​(K))n​[1]⊕𝔽(0)n+1H_{*}(\widehat{A}_{0}(K))^{n+1}\oplus\mathbb{F}^{n}_{(-1)}\cong H_{*}(\widehat{A}_{0}(K))^{n}[1]\oplus\mathbb{F}^{n+1}_{(0)}

cannot possibly hold.

In the case where ν⁡(K)=0\nu(K)=0, we force a relatively graded isomorphism

Kn⊕𝔽(0)≅K​[1]m⊕𝔽(0),K^{n}\oplus\mathbb{F}_{(0)}\cong K[1]^{m}\oplus\mathbb{F}_{(0)},

where here KK is the kernel of the map on homology

(v^0⊕h^0)∗:H∗​(A^0)⟶𝔽⊕𝔽.(\widehat{v}_{0}\oplus\widehat{h}_{0})_{*}\colon H_{*}(\widehat{A}_{0})\longrightarrow\mathbb{F}\oplus\mathbb{F}.

Such a relatively graded isomorphism can hold only if the rank of KK is zero. In turn, this forces rk​H∗​(A^0)=1\mathrm{rk}H_{*}(\widehat{A}_{0})=1. From Proposition 9.6, it follows now that KK is a trivial knot, contradicting our hypothesis.           

By Proposition 9.5 (or alternatively [16]), a genus one knot with LL-space surgeries is easily seen to have the knot Floer homology groups of the trefoil TT. In particular, if Sr3​(K)≅Ss3​(K)S^{3}_{r}(K)\cong S^{3}_{s}(K), then it follows that H​F+​(Sr3​(T))≅H​F+​(Sr3​(T))HF^{+}(S^{3}_{r}(T))\cong HF^{+}(S^{3}_{r}(T)) as ℚ\mathbb{Q}-graded groups. Of course, H​F+​(Sr3​(T))HF^{+}(S^{3}_{r}(T)) can be calculated explicitly (for example using Theorem 1.2), and the authors know of no pair of distinct rational numbers rr and ss for which H​F+​(Sr3​(T))≅H​F+​(Ss3​(T))HF^{+}(S^{3}_{r}(T))\cong HF^{+}(S^{3}_{s}(T)).

In a different direction, the algebra can be used in some cases to exclude cosmetic surgeries with a fixed numerator pp (i.e. first homology of the surgered manifold). We content ourselves here with a discussion of the case where p=3p=3.

Theorem 9.10.

Suppose that KK is a non-trivial knot. Then, if r,s∈ℚr,s\in\mathbb{Q} both with numerators having absolute value 33, and with r≠sr\neq s, we have that Sr3​(K)≇Ss3​(K)S^{3}_{r}(K)\not\cong S^{3}_{s}(K) as oriented manifolds.

Proof. By Lemma 9.2, we can arrange that ν⁡(K)≥0\nu(K)\geq 0. The possibility that ν⁡(K)≥3\nu(K)\geq 3 is excluded by counting ranks. According to Proposition 9.5, we have that

H​F^(S−3/q3(K))=3+q⋅(2(2ν(K)−1)+∑s(rkH∗(A^s)−1)).\widehat{HF}(S^{3}_{-3/q}(K))=3+q\cdot\left(2(2\nu(K)-1)+\sum_{s}\left(\mathrm{rk}H_{*}(\widehat{A}_{s})-1\right)\right).

When ν⁡(K)≥3\nu(K)\geq 3, then for all qq, we have that

(34) 6≤(2​ν−1)​q,6\leq(2\nu-1)q,

and hence

H​F​(S3/q3​(K))=−3+q⋅(2​(2​ν​(K)−1)+∑s(r​k​H∗​(A^s)−1)).HF(S^{3}_{3/q}(K))=-3+q\cdot\left(2(2\nu(K)-1)+\sum_{s}\left(rkH_{*}(\widehat{A}_{s})-1\right)\right).

10. Seifert fibered spaces

Methods from this paper lead to the calculation of the Heegaard Floer homology groups of a large class of Seifert fibered spaces. The primary ingredients here are the calculation of the knot Floer homology of the “Borromean knot” (c.f. Section  of [22]), the knot Oq/rO_{q/r} considered in Section 7, and Theorem 6.1. Our aim here is to state and prove these results.

Let h:ℤ⟶ℤh\colon\mathbb{Z}\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z} be a function with the property that

lims↦±∞h⁡(s)=+∞.\lim_{s\mapsto\pm\infty}h(s)=+\infty.

We describe here a natural ℤ⁡[U]\mathbb{Z}[U]-module associated to XX. It is interesting to compare the following construction with a construction of Némethi [12], see also [19].

A well at height n≥0n\geq 0 is a pair of integers (i,j)(i,j) with i<j−2i<j-2 and the property that h⁡(k)≤nh(k)\leq n for all i≤k≤ji\leq k\leq j, while h⁡(i)>nh(i)>n and h⁡(j)>nh(j)>n. Let Mn​(h)M_{n}(h) denote the free Abelian group generated by Wn​(h)W_{n}(h).

If x∈Wn​(h)x\in W_{n}(h) and y∈Wn−1​(h)y\in W_{n-1}(h), we write x>yx>y if x=(i,j)x=(i,j) and y=(i′,j′)y=(i^{\prime},j^{\prime}) with i≤i′<j′≤ji\leq i^{\prime}<j^{\prime}\leq j. Define U:Wn​(h)⟶Wn−1​(h)U\colon W_{n}(h)\longrightarrow W_{n-1}(h) by the formula

U⋅x=∑{y∈Wn−1​(h)|x>y}y,U\cdot x=\sum_{\{y\in W_{n-1}(h)\big|x>y\}}y,

and let

ℍ​𝔽+​(h)=⨁n∈ℤWn​(h)\mathbb{HF}^{+}(h)=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}W_{n}(h)

be the induced module over ℤ⁡[U]\mathbb{Z}[U]. Indeed, we can view this as a graded ℤ⁡[U]\mathbb{Z}[U] module by the grading which sends Wn​(h)W_{n}(h) to 2​n2n.

In the language of Némethi, the set of wells forms a root, and ℍ​𝔽+​(h)\mathbb{HF}^{+}(h) is the associated ℤ⁡[U]\mathbb{Z}[U]-module.

Let YY be a Seifert fibered space over a genus gg orbifold with Seifert invariants (a,r1/q1,…,rn/qn)(a,r_{1}/q_{1},...,r_{n}/q_{n}) over a genus gg base, c.f. [29], [28], [7]. The orbifold degree is the quantity

deg⁡(Y)=a+∑iriqi.\deg(Y)=a+\sum_{i}\frac{r_{i}}{q_{i}}.

Recall that b1​(Y)b_{1}(Y) is even if and only if deg⁡(Y)≠0\deg(Y)\neq 0. By reversing the orientation on YY, we can arrange for deg⁡(Y)>0\deg(Y)>0.

There is a presentation of the first homology of YY as

H1​(Y,ℤ)\displaystyle H_{1}(Y;\mathbb{Z}) ≅\displaystyle{\cong} H1​(Σ,ℤ)⊕ℤ​m0⊕ℤ​m1⊕…⊕ℤ​mn(a⋅m0+∑i=1nri⋅mi=0,ri⋅m0−qi⋅mi=0,i=1,…,n)\displaystyle\frac{H_{1}(\Sigma;\mathbb{Z})\oplus\mathbb{Z}m_{0}\oplus\mathbb{Z}m_{1}\oplus...\oplus\mathbb{Z}m_{n}}{\left(\begin{array}[]{ll}a\cdot m_{0}+\sum_{i=1}^{n}r_{i}\cdot m_{i}=0,&\\ r_{i}\cdot m_{0}-q_{i}\cdot m_{i}=0,&i=1,...,n\end{array}\right)}

(c.f. below for more specifics).

Theorem 10.1.

Let YY be a Seifert fibered space over a genus gg orbifold with positive degree, and Seifert invariants (a,r1/q1,…,rn/qn)(a,r_{1}/q_{1},...,r_{n}/q_{n}). There is an affine identification Spinc​(Y)≅H1​(Y,ℤ){\mathrm{Spin}}^{c}(Y)\cong H_{1}(Y;\mathbb{Z}) with the following properties.

  • •

For integers −g≤t≤g-g\leq t\leq g, let δt:ℤ⟶ℤ\delta_{t}\colon\mathbb{Z}\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z} be the function defined by

    and ht:ℤ⟶ℤh_{t}\colon\mathbb{Z}\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z} be the function

    ht​(s)={∑i=0s−1δt​(i)if s≥0−∑i=s−1δt(i)if s<0.h_{t}(s)=\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\sum_{i=0}^{s-1}\delta_{t}(i)&{\text{if $s\geq 0$}}\\ -\sum_{i=s}^{-1}\delta_{t}(i)&{\text{if $s<0$.}}\end{array}\right.

    Then, there is a relatively ℤ\mathbb{Z}-graded isomorphism of ℤ⁡[U]\mathbb{Z}[U]-modules:

    (39) H​F+​(Y,𝔰)≅⨁−g≤t≤gΛg+t​H1​(Σ,ℤ)⊗ℤℍ​𝔽+​(ht).HF^{+}(Y,\mathfrak{s})\cong\bigoplus_{-g\leq t\leq g}\Lambda^{g+t}H_{1}(\Sigma;\mathbb{Z})\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{HF}^{+}(h_{t}).

In the above statement, the tensor product is to be taken in the graded sense: Λg+t​H1​(Σ,ℤ)\Lambda^{g+t}H_{1}(\Sigma;\mathbb{Z}) is supported in grading tt. Note also that the right-hand-side is graded only in the relative sense, corresponding to our choice of 𝔰\mathfrak{s}.

Note that in the case where g=0g=0, this recaptures (as a relatively ℤ\mathbb{Z}-graded group) the description of H​F+HF^{+} for rational homology Seifert fibered spaces given by Némethi in terms of his “computational sequences”. We prove Theorem 10.1 in Subsection 10.2 below, after giving some sample calculations.

Although we have described here the Floer homology only as a relatively graded group, the absolute grading can be obtained by comparing the summand corresponding to t=0t=0 with the calculation of genus zero Seifert fibered spaces from [19], see also [12].

10.2. Proof of Theorem 10.1.

It is useful to have a mild generalization of the rational surgeries formula.

Definition 10.2.

Let K⊂YK\subset Y be a null-homologous knot in a three-manifold YY. Fix an integer aa and an nn-tuple of rational numbers {qiri}i=1n\{\frac{q_{i}}{r_{i}}\}_{i=1}^{n}. Consider an nn-tuple of unknotted circles OiO_{i} each of which links KK once, and which are pairwise mutually unlinked. Let Y⁡(K,a,{qi/ri}i=1n)Y(K,a,\{q_{i}/r_{i}\}_{i=1}^{n}) denote the three-manifold obtained as aa-surgery on KK, followed by −qiri-\frac{q_{i}}{r_{i}} surgery on each OiO_{i}. This three-manifold Y⁡(K,a,{qi/ri}i=1n)Y(K,a,\{q_{i}/r_{i}\}_{i=1}^{n}) is said to be obtained as a generalized rational surgery on K⊂YK\subset Y, with Seifert invariants (a,{qi/ri}i=1n)(a,\{q_{i}/r_{i}\}_{i=1}^{n}).

For fixed K⊂YK\subset Y, let

Y′=Y​#​(#i=1n​L​(qi,ri))\displaystyle Y^{\prime}=Y\#\left(\#_{i=1}^{n}L(q_{i},r_{i})\right) and K′=K​#​(#i=1n​Oqi/ri)\displaystyle K^{\prime}=K\#\left(\#_{i=1}^{n}O_{q_{i}/r_{i}}\right)

in the notation of Section 7. Of course, Y⁡(K,a,{qi/ri}i=1n)Y(K,a,\{q_{i}/r_{i}\}_{i=1}^{n}) can be thought of as the three-manifold gotten by aa-surgery on K′⊂Y′K^{\prime}\subset Y^{\prime}.

As an example, if we start with the unknot K⊂S3K\subset S^{3} and form the three-manifold S3​(K,a,{qi/ri}i=1n)S^{3}(K,a,\{q_{i}/r_{i}\}_{i=1}^{n}), we obtain the Seifert fibered space whose base has genus zero, nn singular fibers, and Seifert invariants (a,{qi/ri}i=1n)(a,\{q_{i}/r_{i}\}_{i=1}^{n}), with the standard conventions. More generally, if we start with the Borromean knot Bg⊂#2​g​(S1×S2)B_{g}\subset\#^{2g}(S^{1}\times S^{2}) (this is the knot obtained by taking zero surgery on two of the components of the Borromean rings to obtain a knot B1B_{1} in #2​(S1×S2)\#^{2}(S^{1}\times S^{2}), and then taking the connected sum of gg copies of B1B_{1}) , the resulting three-manifold #2​g​(S1×S2)​(Bg,a,{qi/ri}i=1n)\#^{2g}(S^{1}\times S^{2})(B_{g},a,\{q_{i}/r_{i}\}_{i=1}^{n}) is the Seifert space over a genus gg base orbifold with Seifert invariants (a,{qi/ri}i=1n)(a,\{q_{i}/r_{i}\}_{i=1}^{n}).

Of course,

H1​(Y′,ℤ)≅H1​(Y−K,ℤ)⊕ℤ​m1⊕…⊕ℤ​mn(a⋅m0+∑i=1nmi=0,ri⋅m0−qi⋅mi=0,i=1,…,m),H_{1}(Y^{\prime};\mathbb{Z})\cong\frac{H_{1}(Y-K;\mathbb{Z})\oplus\mathbb{Z}m_{1}\oplus...\oplus\mathbb{Z}m_{n}}{\left(\begin{array}[]{ll}a\cdot m_{0}+\sum_{i=1}^{n}m_{i}=0,&\\ r_{i}\cdot m_{0}-q_{i}\cdot m_{i}=0,&i=1,...,m\end{array}\right)},

where here m0∈H1​(Y−K,ℤ)m_{0}\in H_{1}(Y-K;\mathbb{Z}) denotes the homology class of the meridian of KK. We can change basis, letting gi=ai⋅m0+bi⋅mig_{i}=a_{i}\cdot m_{0}+b_{i}\cdot m_{i}, where here ai⋅qi+ri⋅bi=1a_{i}\cdot q_{i}+r_{i}\cdot b_{i}=1, to obtain a presentation

H1​(Y′,ℤ)≅H1​(Y−K,ℤ)⊕ℤ​g1⊕…⊕ℤ​gn(a⋅m0+∑i=1nri⋅gi=0,m0−qi⋅gi=0,i=1,…,m).H_{1}(Y^{\prime};\mathbb{Z})\cong\frac{H_{1}(Y-K;\mathbb{Z})\oplus\mathbb{Z}g_{1}\oplus...\oplus\mathbb{Z}g_{n}}{\left(\begin{array}[]{ll}a\cdot m_{0}+\sum_{i=1}^{n}r_{i}\cdot g_{i}=0,&\\ m_{0}-q_{i}\cdot g_{i}=0,&i=1,...,m\end{array}\right)}.

Consider the map

β:H1​(Y′−K′,ℤ)⟶H1​(Y−K,ℤ)\beta\colon H_{1}(Y^{\prime}-K^{\prime};\mathbb{Z})\longrightarrow H_{1}(Y-K;\mathbb{Z})

Proposition 10.3.

Let K⊂YK\subset Y be a null-homologous knot, and fix an E∈Spinc​(Y′−K′)E\in{\mathrm{Spin}}^{c}(Y^{\prime}-K^{\prime}). Suppose moreover that b1​(Y⁡(K,a,{qi/ri}))=b1​(Y)b_{1}(Y(K,a,\{q_{i}/r_{i}\}))=b_{1}(Y). There is a map f:H1(Y′−K′)⟶Spinc(Y(K,a,{qi/ri])f\colon H_{1}(Y^{\prime}-K^{\prime})\longrightarrow{\mathrm{Spin}}^{c}(Y(K,a,\{q_{i}/r_{i}]) with the property that for each E∈Y′−K′E\in Y^{\prime}-K^{\prime} for which c1​(f​(E))c_{1}(f(E)) is a torsion class, we have that H​F+​(Y⁡(K,a,{qi/ri}i=1n),f⁡(E))HF^{+}(Y(K,a,\{q_{i}/r_{i}\}_{i=1}^{n}),f(E)) is identified with the homology of the mapping cone D[E]+:𝔸[E]+⟶𝔹[E]+D^{+}_{[E]}\colon{\mathbb{A}}^{+}_{[E]}\longrightarrow{\mathbb{B}}^{+}_{[E]}.

Proof. Like Theorem 1.1, this follows from a direct application of Theorems 6.1,  5.1, and the calculation of the invariant for Oq/r⊂L⁡(q,r)O_{q/r}\subset L(q,r) of Lemma 7.1.           

Theorem 10.1 follows quickly from Proposition 10.3, together with the calculation of the knot Floer homology of the Borromean knot (c.f. Section  of [22]), which we summarize here:

Lemma 10.4.

Let K⊂#2​g​(S2×S1)K\subset\#^{2g}(S^{2}\times S^{1}) be the Borromean knot. The Spinc{\mathrm{Spin}}^{c} structure over #2​g​(S2×S1)\#^{2g}(S^{2}\times S^{1}) with trivial first Chern class is the only one whose induced knot filtration consists of non-zero groups. For that chain complex CC, we have a splitting

(40) C≅⨁tΛt+g​H1​(Σ,ℤ)⊗ℤℤ⁡[U,U−1],C\cong\bigoplus_{t}\Lambda^{t+g}H_{1}(\Sigma;\mathbb{Z})\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Z}[U,U^{-1}],

where this splitting corresponds to the various summands C{i−j=t}C\{i-j=t\}. In particular, there are identifications

Λt+g​H1​(Σ,ℤ)⊗ℤ𝒯+→Umax⁡(0,s−t)Λt+g​H1​(Σ,ℤ)⊗ℤ𝒯+→≅Λ−t+g​H1​(Σ,ℤ)⊗ℤ𝒯+↓↓As+→h+B+→=B+,\begin{CD}\Lambda^{t+g}H_{1}(\Sigma;\mathbb{Z})\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}{\mathcal{T}}^{+}@>{U^{\max(0,s-t)}}>{}>\Lambda^{t+g}H_{1}(\Sigma;\mathbb{Z})\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}{\mathcal{T}}^{+}@>{\cong}>{}>\Lambda^{-t+g}H_{1}(\Sigma;\mathbb{Z})\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}{\mathcal{T}}^{+}\\ @V{}V{}V&&@V{}V{}V\\ {A}^{+}_{s}@>{h^{+}}>{}>{B}^{+}@>{=}>{}>{B}^{+},\end{CD}

where here all the vertical maps are induced by inclusions in the identification of Equation (40).

Proof. Most of the above statements are a direct result of Proposition  of [22], which, together with the Künneth principle, gives that

C⁡{i,j}=U−i⊗Λg−i+j​H1​(Σ,ℤ),C\{i,j\}=U^{-i}\otimes\Lambda^{g-i+j}H^{1}(\Sigma;\mathbb{Z}),

with no differentials. The second square involves the identification between C{i≥0}C\{i\geq 0\} and C{j≥0}C\{j\geq 0\}, which is sends the subset C{i−j=t}C\{i-j=t\} to C{i−j=−t}C\{i-j=-t\}, as explained in Proposition  of [25].

Proof. The map DδD_{\delta} is surjective. It remains to identify its kernel. Given (i,j)∈Wn​(h)(i,j)\in W_{n}(h), consider the element {as}s∈ℤ\{a_{s}\}_{s\in\mathbb{Z}} defined by the property that

as={(−1)k​Uh⁡(k)−nif i<k<j0otherwise.a_{s}=\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}(-1)^{k}U^{h(k)-n}&{\text{if $i<k<j$}}\\ 0&{\text{otherwise.}}\end{array}\right.

By linearity, we can extend this to a homomorphism Wn​(h)⟶Ker​DδW_{n}(h)\longrightarrow\mathrm{Ker}D_{\delta}. It is straightforward to verify that this extends to an isomorphism ℍ​𝔽+​(h)⟶Ker​Dδ\mathbb{HF}^{+}(h)\longrightarrow\mathrm{Ker}D_{\delta}.           

Proof of Theorem 10.1. According to the adjunction inequality (c.f. Theorem  of [23]), since the Thurston norm of YY is trivial, it follows that H​F+​(Y,𝔰)HF^{+}(Y,\mathfrak{s}) is trivial for all Spinc{\mathrm{Spin}}^{c} structures with non-torsion c1​(𝔰)c_{1}(\mathfrak{s}). According to the combination of Proposition 10.3 and Lemma 10.4, given EE, the Floer homology H​F+​(Y,[E])HF^{+}(Y,[E]) splits as

H​F+​(Y,[E])≅⨁t∈ℤΛg+t​H1​(Σ,ℤ)⊗ℤX⁡(t),HF^{+}(Y,[E])\cong\bigoplus_{t\in\mathbb{Z}}\Lambda^{g+t}H^{1}(\Sigma;\mathbb{Z})\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}X(t),

where here X⁡(t)X(t) is the homology of a chain complex satisfying the hypotheses of Lemma 10.5, for the function δt:ℤ⟶ℤ\delta_{t}\colon\mathbb{Z}\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z} as in the statement of the theorem. The theorem now follows from the calculation in Lemma 10.5. Note that Equation (41) holds, since the orbifold has positive degree. ∎
